candidates.name: Varicella zoster vasculopathy
support_spans: Numerous 3- to 6-mm pseudovesicular papules with superficial crusting were noted on the trunk.
Within 48 hours the papules evolved to an extensive, but not confluent, purpuric rash.
contradict_spans: Diagnostic testing on superficial skin sample for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 viruses (all negative)
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and skin lesions are consistent with a varicella zoster infection, despite negative diagnostic tests.

candidates.name: Petechial rash due to sepsis
support_spans: Within 48 hours the papules evolved to an extensive, but not confluent, purpuric rash.
Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis
candidates.why: The patient's purpuric rash and laboratory results could be indicative of sepsis.

candidates.name: Disseminated varicella zoster virus infection
support_spans: Numerous 3- to 6-mm pseudovesicular papules with superficial crusting were noted on the trunk.
Histologic analysis showed: - Extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis- Large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration
contradict_spans: Diagnostic testing on superficial skin sample for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 viruses (all negative)
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and histologic analysis are consistent with a disseminated varicella zoster virus infection, despite negative diagnostic tests.

candidates.name: Vasculitis due to autoimmune response
support_spans: Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis
Early-stage vasculitic alterations with endothelial swelling of dermal vessels without fibrinoid necrosis or thrombosis
candidates.why: The patient's laboratory results and histologic analysis could be indicative of an autoimmune response leading to vasculitis.
